seoTitle: Custom Logo Perfume: Private Label Guide | TopPerfume
description: Plan a custom logo perfume order: compare branding options, prepare your artwork, confirm MOQ and samples, and send a clear brief for a private label quote.
excerpt: Learn what to confirm before adding your logo to a fragrance product, from eligible packaging and artwork to quantity, sampling and a written quotation.
title: Custom Logo Perfume: A Private Label Buying Guide
html:
A perfume with your logo starts with a few practical decisions: which product you want to sell, where your branding should appear, and what needs to be approved before production. Getting those decisions clear makes the first quotation more useful—and gives you a better basis for comparing options.

This guide is for retailers and new beauty brands planning a fragrance project. It explains how to prepare a brief, separate different types of customization, and move from an idea to a sample and quotation.

Choose the buying route that matches your plan

Begin by deciding whether you want to purchase finished products for resale or develop a product under your own brand. The available products, minimum quantities and approval steps can differ.

Buying route What you are asking for What to confirm first
Finished-product wholesale An existing product for your retail assortment Exact product reference, quantity, packaging and current availability
Your logo on an eligible product Your brand identity applied through an agreed branding route Product eligibility, logo position, available method and minimum quantity
A wider development project Changes to packaging, fragrance direction or other product details Feasible scope, samples, separate costs and project timing

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner, reviewing custom projects with suppliers individually. Our low-MOQ perfume and private-label page sets out the current routes. Its starting quantities apply to eligible options; the final scope is confirmed against your brief.

If you are browsing finished products carrying an existing brand, ask us to identify an appropriate private-label option for your project. Buying a branded wholesale product and commissioning your own branded product are separate requests.

Decide where your logo should appear

Think about how a customer will see and handle the product. The bottle is one part of the presentation; the carton, label and other agreed packaging elements may also carry your brand information.

Prepare a simple placement list. For each part, identify what you want to show: the brand name, product name, design element or other approved text. Ask which branding methods are available for the selected component before fixing the artwork.

Questions worth resolving early include:

  • Is the proposed logo position suitable for this bottle or packaging surface?
  • What usable area and artwork dimensions should the designer work to?
  • Which colours and finishes are available for this specific option?
  • Will the quotation cover the bottle branding, outer box or both?
  • What additional product information must be accommodated in the final artwork for the intended market?

Treat a reference image as a way to explain your preferred direction. The agreed specification and approved sample should identify what will actually be supplied.

Prepare the product brief before polishing the design

A useful first message describes the business and product decisions as well as the logo. You can begin while some choices are still open: mark them as questions so the quotation addresses them directly.

Brief field What to include
Business and customers Your shop or brand, target customers and sales channel
Product direction Perfume, fragrance mist or another requested format; preferred size
Fragrance direction Your description of the scent you want to explore, if relevant
Branding scope Bottle, label, carton or other requested elements
Quantity Estimated units, with a breakdown by product or version
Artwork status Logo available, artwork in progress, or guidance requested
Destination Country and city for the shipping discussion
Timing Your preferred launch date and any fixed deadline
Budget A purchasing budget or target cost, if you have one

For example, “one fragrance product with our logo on the bottle and carton” is a clearer starting scope than “fully custom perfume.” It allows the supplier to explain what is available and which decisions still affect the quotation.

Confirm how the minimum quantity is counted

Ask whether the minimum applies per fragrance, bottle size, packaging version or artwork design. A quantity spread across several versions may be treated differently from the same quantity of one confirmed item.

TopPerfume’s current route page lists selected logo and private-label options from 100 pieces. This is a starting point for eligible projects. Ask for the minimum quantity and available configuration for the exact product you are discussing.

Also ask what changes if you revise the bottle, fragrance, decoration or outer packaging. A finished-product wholesale minimum should not be used to budget a different custom project.

Review artwork and samples in separate steps

An artwork layout helps you review placement and text. A physical sample allows you to inspect the supplied materials and appearance. Ask which type of sample is available at each stage and what it represents.

Before approving the project, review:

  • The correct brand spelling, product wording and agreed artwork version.
  • Logo size, position and appearance on the selected component.
  • The bottle, cap and packaging configuration included in the quotation.
  • The selected fragrance sample or product reference, where applicable.
  • Any differences between the sample and the proposed bulk order.

Keep the approval record specific. Use a dated reference and an agreed list of components, rather than relying on a general “looks good” message. Ask for sample charges and shipping costs to be stated before proceeding.

Request a quotation with an agreed scope

Your quotation should identify the product, quantity, branding work and packaging included. Ask whether there are separate artwork, setup, sample or shipping charges, and which costs remain to be confirmed.

Discuss the timeline as stages: specification confirmation, artwork approval, sample review and dispatch planning. The applicable timing depends on the selected project. A general website dispatch indication should not become a fixed arrival promise for an unconfirmed custom order.

For repeat orders, ask how the approved specification will be referenced and whether availability, quantity requirements or pricing need to be reconfirmed.

Questions buyers often ask

Can I start by adding a logo without developing a new fragrance?

Ask about the existing options eligible for your own branding. Your logo brief can be reviewed separately from a new fragrance-development request; availability is confirmed by product and supplier.

Do I need finished artwork before contacting you?

You can start with a product direction, estimated quantity and preferred logo position. State whether your logo is ready and request the applicable artwork requirements before preparing the final layout.

Can I split the order across several designs?

Include the proposed quantity for each version in your brief. The minimum and setup arrangements must be checked for that configuration.

Does a catalogue product automatically support my own logo?

Customization eligibility is reviewed separately. Identify the product or format you like and ask which private-label options are suitable.

Discuss your custom logo perfume project

Send your product direction, logo placement, estimated quantity and destination through the TopPerfume contact page. If some details are undecided, include those questions in the brief.

You can also compare the existing wholesale and private-label routes before requesting a quotation. The aim of the first conversation is to identify a suitable product and a clear scope for the next decision.

seoTitle: Wholesale Perfume for a New Store: Guide | TopPerfume
description: Plan your first wholesale perfume order with a clear customer profile, sample shortlist, SKU quantities, cost comparison and supplier questions before you buy.
excerpt: Build a focused first fragrance order by matching products to your customers, comparing samples and confirming product-by-product buying terms.
title: Buying Wholesale Perfume for a New Store: Your First-Order Guide
html:
Your first perfume order shapes what customers see, what your team can explain and how much money is committed to stock. Before adding more products, give each item a clear reason to be in the assortment.

This guide helps new fragrance shops, beauty retailers and online sellers prepare a focused wholesale order. Start with your customers, build a shortlist, compare samples and confirm the terms for each product before committing to quantities.

Describe the customer you want to serve

Write a short buying brief for your store. Include who you expect to buy, how they will discover the products and the type of purchase you want to support.

For example, are you planning a gift-focused display, adding fragrance to an existing beauty shop or opening an online assortment with a few clearly differentiated choices? These are planning directions, rather than predictions of what will sell.

Record four starting points:

  • Your customers and sales channel.
  • The intended retail price range.
  • Product formats and sizes you want to consider.
  • The amount you can allocate to stock, samples and delivery.

When you discuss options with a supplier, this brief helps explain why one product may fit your plan better than another.

Give each shortlisted product a role

You can build a small assortment around distinct customer preferences or shopping occasions. Ask for the product information and samples needed to evaluate each choice.

A planning sheet might look like this:

Role in the assortment Candidate product Question to resolve before buying Planned quantity
An everyday fragrance option Add a product link Does the sample fit the customer preference you are targeting? Decide after review
A different scent direction Add a product link Is the difference clear enough to explain to a customer? Decide after review
A gift-focused option Add a product link Are the presentation, size and total cost suitable? Decide after review
A possible later addition Keep a reference What evidence would justify adding this product? Leave out of the first order if undecided

The rows are a planning example, not a fixed bundle or a recommendation to stock four specific products. Use only the roles that make sense for your business.

Browse the TopPerfume fragrance collection to identify actual product references. Where fragrance notes or other details are not listed, ask for the information rather than inferring it from the bottle colour or product name.

Compare samples before deciding the full quantity

For each sample, record the product name, size and the reference supplied. Keep scent preference separate from packaging observations so you can explain why you prefer one option.

You may want to compare:

  • Your impression of the fragrance and how it develops during your observation.
  • How you would describe it to your intended customers.
  • The spray, cap, bottle and packaging as received.
  • Whether the supplied product information answers your retail questions.

Use reasonably consistent conditions when comparing samples, and record the time and context of any longevity observations. Your own sample notes support a buying decision; they are not a substitute for substantiated product performance claims.

Ask the supplier to clarify any mismatch between the sample, the product description and the proposed bulk supply before proceeding.

Confirm buying terms product by product

A low minimum advertised for one item does not establish the minimum for an entire catalogue. Check the exact SKU and any variants you want to order.

For example, the Lattafa Khamrah 100 mL product page provides an individual product reference and its listed order terms. Use the current page and a written quotation for that item, then repeat the check for each additional product.

Ask these questions:

  1. What is the current minimum for this exact product or variant?
  2. Can my proposed order contain different products, and what minimum applies to each?
  3. Is the requested quantity available for the planned order?
  4. What packaging is included with the quoted item?
  5. What sample, dispatch and delivery arrangements apply?

If your plan includes your own logo, describe it as a separate project. TopPerfume’s wholesale and private-label routes have different starting points and require product-specific confirmation.

Compare the cost of getting the order to your business

Keep the product subtotal separate from the full purchasing cost. Use the actual quotation for your destination and scope.

Cost item What to record
Products Unit price multiplied by the agreed quantity for each item
Samples Any agreed sample and sample-shipping charges
Extra work Agreed branding, packaging or other project charges, if applicable
Freight and handling The quoted transport scope and any stated exclusions
Other applicable charges Amounts confirmed for your transaction and destination

Compare suppliers on the same product specification, quantities and included services. If an amount is unknown, keep it visible as an item to confirm rather than treating it as zero.

TopPerfume’s order information explains that listed product subtotals exclude shipping and taxes and that transaction arrangements are agreed for each order.

Plan how you will explain the products

A useful assortment gives you clear information to share with shoppers. Prepare a short product card for each selected item using confirmed details.

Include the name, size, product presentation and any verified fragrance information. Add your own sample observations where appropriate, clearly identified as observations. If a customer asks about a detail you have not confirmed, return to the supplier for the information.

For online selling, use product images that match what you will supply. For a physical display, consider how the packaging and product information will help customers compare the choices. This preparation also reveals gaps before you purchase the full assortment.

Keep a simple first-order and reorder record

After launch, track what customers ask about, what sells and what remains in stock. Separate sales from interest: a product receiving questions may still need better information, a different presentation or further sample review.

Before placing the first order, ask how to identify the same product for a repeat purchase, how availability is confirmed and what buying terms may change. Keep the supplier reference and agreed specification with your order record.

Use your early results to decide whether to reorder, adjust quantities or add another product. A new item should have a clear role in the assortment.

Questions new buyers often ask

How many perfume products should a new store start with?

There is no fixed count in this guide. Choose a number you can sample, explain and fund within your plan. The planning sheet helps you give each selected product a purpose.

Can I mix different perfumes in one order?

Send the proposed product list and quantity for each item. Mixed-order eligibility and minimum quantities need to be confirmed against those products.

Should I begin with wholesale products or my own brand?

Decide what your first launch requires. Finished-product wholesale and a private-label project involve different product choices, quantities and approvals. Compare the actual options against your customers, budget and timing.

What information should I send to get a useful quote?

Include your destination, product links, quantity per item, planned timing and any sample or customization request. Mention the questions you still need help resolving.

Prepare your first wholesale perfume enquiry

Choose your candidates from the fragrance collection, then contact TopPerfume with your first-order brief.

Information Your first-order brief
Store type and customers Describe your business and intended buyers
Destination Country and city
Product references Paste the selected product links
Quantities List units for each product or variant
Samples State what you want to review first
Branding Standard wholesale or a separate logo/custom project
Timing and open questions Add your preferred schedule and what needs clarification

TopPerfume supports wholesale beauty sourcing and supplier coordination. Sharing a focused brief makes it easier to review product options, confirm the applicable terms and prepare the next step for your order.

seoTitle: Compare Perfume Samples for Wholesale | TopPerfume
description: Compare perfume samples before a wholesale order. Record scent observations, spray and packaging checks, sample costs and questions in a practical buyer worksheet.
excerpt: Compare a fragrance shortlist with a blank observation worksheet, clear sample references and separate checks for scent, packaging and buying terms.
title: How to Compare Perfume Samples Before a Wholesale Order
html:
A perfume sample can help you decide what belongs in your shop, but a good first impression is only one part of the buying decision. You also need to know which product you received, how you compared it and which details still need a supplier's answer.

Use this guide to turn a shortlist into a recorded comparison. It is a retail buying worksheet, not a laboratory test or a promise about fragrance performance. Start with the products in your wholesale perfume shortlist, then keep observations separate from the facts supplied with each sample.

Identify every sample before comparing it

Give each sample a reference that you can use in notes, photographs and follow-up messages. Record the product name, supplier reference, date received and the size stated on the supplied label. If a batch or lot reference is present, copy it exactly; leave missing details unresolved.

Ask what the sample represents. A small fragrance vial may let you explore a scent, while a finished retail unit also lets you inspect its bottle, sprayer and carton. Neither should automatically be treated as approval of every component in a future order.

For example, the Lattafa Khamrah product page identifies a particular branded wholesale product. Ask about a sample of that exact reference and its current availability. It is not a proposal to put your logo on the branded product.

Before paying, confirm the sample reference, quantity, sample charge, shipping charge and destination. Sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer.

Separate scent preference from other buying criteria

Avoid reducing the entire decision to one score. A sample may match your shop's scent direction but have unresolved packaging details. Another may be well presented yet overlap too closely with a product you already sell.

Comparison area What to record What the note does not establish
Scent direction Your own description and the customer preference it might suit A verified ingredient list or an official scent-note specification
Perceived intensity How noticeable it seems under the conditions you record A universal projection or strength rating
Change over time Your observations at named times during the comparison A guaranteed wear duration for every customer
Spray and handling What you observe from the supplied sprayer, cap and bottle The condition of an entire future shipment
Packaging Visible condition, supplied components and label references Confirmation of uninspected packaging or a custom version
Commercial fit The questions about quantity, cost and replenishment that remain Current stock, an agreed bulk quote or a delivery commitment

Keep comparison conditions as consistent as practical

Choose a manageable group of samples and use a separate, clearly labelled fragrance blotter for each. Follow the supplied product instructions. Record how you applied each sample and keep the blotters separate so that your notes refer to the intended product.

Decide when you will revisit the samples and write down the actual observation times. Compare them in a similar setting, noting changes such as moving rooms or returning after a break. If the application method or surroundings differ, record the difference instead of presenting the observations as directly equivalent.

Describe what you notice in ordinary language. “Still noticeable on this blotter at this observation time” is more useful than a broad claim that the perfume lasts all day. If you also record personal wear observations from normal use, keep them separate from the blotter notes and identify the context. Neither record replaces product testing or supports a universal performance claim.

Keep individual feedback before discussing the result

If several buyers or colleagues compare the same shortlist, ask each person to record their impression before discussing a shared decision. Keep differing preferences visible. Your aim is to understand the assortment you want to buy, not to invent a unanimous test result.

Check the sample's physical presentation

Inspect the parcel and supplied components when they arrive. Photograph the item reference and any visible damage before separating the packaging. For a finished bottle, record the sprayer's observed operation, cap fit, visible leakage and the condition of the bottle and carton.

Send a specific question when something is unclear. “The sample arrived without an outer carton; is a carton included in the quoted retail unit?” gives the supplier something concrete to resolve. Do not silently assume that a sample's presentation is the final bulk specification.

Use a blank sample comparison record

Copy this table for each shortlisted product. Keep photographs and supplier replies under the same sample reference. Enter your own observations; the worksheet contains no preset grades or performance targets.

Record field Your entry
Sample reference and exact product To complete
Supplier reference and date received To complete
Labelled size; batch reference if present To complete
Sample format and components supplied To complete
Intended customer and assortment role To complete
Application method, setting and observation times To complete
Scent preference and changes observed To complete
Spray, cap, leakage and packaging observations To complete
Photo references and supplier questions To complete
Sample and freight charges quoted To complete
Decision: shortlist, revisit or decline To complete

Turn observations into a buying decision

Shortlist a sample when you can explain its place in your assortment and identify the remaining commercial questions. Revisit it when the sample reference, package contents or comparison conditions are unclear. Decline it when it does not fit the customer or presentation you are planning.

Before placing a wholesale order, link the selected sample to a written product specification and quote. Confirm the exact product, quantity, supplied packaging, price basis, current availability and dispatch arrangement. Do not treat sample approval as approval of a different size, fragrance or packaging version.

If you are still deciding the range and quantities, use the first wholesale perfume order guide alongside your sample notes.

Send a sample request that can be answered

Tell TopPerfume which products you want to compare, the number of samples requested, your destination and the questions that matter most to your buying decision. Include the expected wholesale quantity separately so that it is not confused with the sample quantity.

Ask for an itemized sample and freight quote before proceeding. TopPerfume coordinates sourcing and supplier discussions; the selected product and current terms need confirmation. You can include your completed worksheet when discussing order terms and your inquiry.

Questions buyers often ask

Does a sample prove how long a perfume will last?

Your record describes what you observed in the stated conditions. It does not prove a fixed wear duration for every person or setting. Ask for relevant product-specific evidence before using a performance claim in your own sales material.

Can I evaluate packaging from a fragrance vial?

A vial does not show the retail bottle, sprayer or carton unless those components are also supplied. Request the appropriate product presentation and confirm any differences before approving an order.

Does paying for a sample reserve wholesale stock?

Do not assume it does. Confirm stock allocation, the final order quantity and the applicable order terms separately with your quotation.

seoTitle: Lip Gloss or Eyeshadow? First Makeup Range | TopPerfume
description: Plan your first makeup collection: compare lip gloss and eyeshadow, organize shades, check sample details and separate wholesale terms from custom project MOQs.
excerpt: Choose a focused lip or eye range, record product and shade requirements, and separate finished-product buying from a custom branding project.
title: Lip Gloss or Eyeshadow? Planning Your First Makeup Collection
html:
Your first makeup collection needs a clear reason for customers to choose it. Start with the look they want, how they shop and the products you can explain well. Then decide whether a focused lip range, an eye palette or a carefully limited combination supports that plan.

This guide helps new brands and beauty retailers build a product and shade brief. It also separates two different requests: buying an existing finished product for resale and developing an eligible product under your own brand. A product in the TopPerfume makeup catalogue is a reference to discuss, not automatic confirmation of private-label eligibility.

Define the customer and the look before choosing products

Write a short description of your intended customer, sales channel and desired makeup finish. A store where customers can compare physical samples needs a different presentation plan from an online launch built around photographs and demonstrations.

Choose the role of each proposed product. It might introduce your colour direction, complement something you already sell or answer a specific request from your audience. Avoid adding shades simply to make the collection appear larger: each extra version creates another quantity, sample and specification to confirm.

Compare what lip gloss and eyeshadow need to show

Neither category is automatically the better first purchase. Compare the information you can obtain and the demonstration you can provide, as well as the appearance of the product itself.

Planning question Lip gloss or lip glaze Eyeshadow or an eye palette
What look are you offering? The selected colour direction, visible finish and coverage to evaluate The colour story, individual finishes and combinations to evaluate
What must a sample show? Appearance, observed texture, applicator and container Individual shades, application observations, pan layout and packaging
What needs a clear identity? Exact product, shade reference and version Exact palette and the shades included; whether it is sold as a fixed unit
What should customers see? Product and shade photographs under recorded conditions The full palette plus identifiable shade images and demonstrations
What remains a supplier question? Net content, ingredients, shade codes, quantities and customization eligibility Net weight, ingredients, shade identities, palette quantities and customization eligibility

The Hydrating Mirror-Shine Lip Glaze and Mocha Chocolate 9-Shade Eyeshadow Palette are two existing catalogue references you can use to start a discussion. The latter is presented as a nine-shade palette. Request the exact sample and available product information before selecting either for your range.

Names and catalogue images help identify the references. They do not establish wear duration, suitability for every skin tone, available custom shades or permission to apply your own logo.

Plan shades around a specific assortment

Describe the colour direction you want and how each proposed shade differs from the others. Use supplier shade codes when confirmed. Until then, mark a reference as provisional and connect it to a photograph or physical sample instead of inventing a code.

A screen image is useful for shortlisting, but it should not be your only colour record. Ask for samples and document the appearance under consistent lighting. Keep the product reference and the conditions attached to your photographs so that later decisions can refer to the same item.

Treat a palette and individual shades as different order units

A palette containing several shades may be supplied as one fixed product. That does not mean each pan can be selected, replaced or ordered separately. Ask whether you are quoting a finished palette, a selection from existing shade options or a separate development request.

For lip products, ask how the quantity is allocated between shades. Do not assume that a minimum for one reference can be divided across every colour shown in a catalogue.

Inspect the packaging before preparing your logo

Record the container, cap or closure, applicator or pan layout and any outer packaging supplied with the sample. Note the usable branding area as a question for the supplier; a visible surface is not proof that a particular printing method is available.

If you want your own brand, submit that as a separate project request. Ask which product options are eligible, what can change and which components the quote includes. Do not commission final artwork around an unconfirmed tube, palette or carton.

TopPerfume works as a trading and sourcing partner. Customization depends on the selected product, supplier and agreed scope. Perfume project minimums should not be transferred to a lip or eye product without confirmation of the applicable makeup project terms.

Ask exactly how the MOQ is counted

Request a written quantity breakdown covering the finished product, shade, packaging version and artwork version where relevant. Keep the finished-product wholesale requirement separate from logo or packaging customization requirements.

For example, an inquiry for several lip shades should list the proposed quantity of each shade, then ask whether the combination is accepted. It is a request for confirmation, not a claim that mixed shades satisfy a supplier's minimum.

Ask for product, customization, sample and freight costs to be identified separately. Sample availability can be confirmed for the selected product or project. Samples are charged, and shipping is paid by the buyer. No single sample charge or makeup customization minimum is assumed in this guide.

Record samples before making launch claims

Keep photographs of the product, shade identity, packaging and your application observations together. Follow the supplied usage instructions. Record the lighting, application method and any differences between comparisons instead of treating every photograph as directly equivalent.

Use observations to decide what to ask next. A preferred finish or texture is a selection note. It does not substantiate waterproof, fixed wear-time, ingredient, vegan or other claims that need product-specific evidence. Ask for the relevant information before putting such claims on packaging or a sales page.

Build a first-collection worksheet

Copy one row for each proposed product or version. Leave unresolved fields open until you have the corresponding sample or supplier response.

Planning field Your entry
Customer, market and sales channel To complete
Product type and role in the collection To complete
Product reference; confirmed shade or palette identity To complete
Desired look and sample observations To complete
Proposed quantity per product and shade To complete
Finished-product purchase or separate custom project To complete
Requested logo or packaging scope; eligibility response To complete
Net content, ingredients and other missing documents To complete
Sample charge and buyer-paid shipping quote To complete
Photo references, open questions and approval status To complete
Destination and preferred launch date To complete

Send a focused brief for the next step

Send your target customer, chosen product direction, shade plan, expected quantities and destination. State whether you want the existing finished product or need TopPerfume to review a separate private-label project. Attach product links so that similar-looking references are not confused.

Discuss timing after the product and customization scope are clear. Lead time depends on the customization scope and project requirements. A preferred launch date is a planning input, not a confirmed production or arrival commitment.

Use the contact and order-terms page to start that discussion with your worksheet and remaining questions.

Questions buyers often ask

Should I launch both lip and eye products at once?

Only include both when you can explain each product's role and confirm the samples, quantities and budget involved. A focused first range can be easier to describe and review; this is a planning choice, not a guaranteed sales outcome.

Can I put my logo on either catalogue reference?

Eligibility for these exact references needs confirmation. Ask for suitable project options and a specific quote. An existing product page or wholesale minimum does not establish customization availability.

Can different shades be combined to meet a minimum?

Submit the proposed breakdown and ask for the accepted allocation in writing. Mixed-shade or mixed-SKU rules must be confirmed for the product or project.
